brief.headline: Aluminium was the strongest metal on the London board on the day the exchange reopened - cash up 1.21% to $3,261.00 while copper fell 0.96% and nickel 2.97% on the same hostile macro - and the cash-to-three-month contango closed entirely to zero, the first time price and curve have moved the same way in this cycle.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The London Metal Exchange reopened after the UK Summer Bank Holiday and printed its first new official in five publishing days. Aluminium cash settled $3,261.00, up $39.00 or +1.21%; three-month $3,261.00, up $20.00 or +0.62%; warehouse stock unchanged at 246,725 tonnes. Because the forward rose less than cash, the $19.00 contango closed completely and the curve is now DEAD FLAT at $0.00. On the same session copper cash fell 0.96%, nickel 2.97% and lead 0.32%, while zinc rose 1.11%. Aluminium led the board.

WHY IT MOVED, AND WHY THE RANKING IS THE EVIDENCE. The macro backdrop was actively hostile to every industrial metal at once: money markets now price roughly a 70% chance of a US rate HIKE on 16-September after the new Fed chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut, the global bond selloff has pushed yields to their highest since 2008, gold has erased its entire 2026 gain, and the wires carried copper falling on demand concerns and nickel at a one-month low. When a shared macro pushes four metals down and one up, the one going up is being bid for something specific. The specific thing is the Gulf: two oil tankers were struck inside the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, the US carried out retaliatory strikes on Iranian tankers, and Brent rose for a third straight session above $95 to a near six-week high. Roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through that waterway. No other metal on the board has that exposure.

WHY TO BE CAREFUL ABOUT IT ANYWAY, AND THIS IS THE PART A ONE-DAY MOVE HIDES. Warehouse stock did not fall by a single tonne - 246,725 t for a third published session, and 200 tonnes in total across thirteen sessions since 17-August. A price and a curve can be moved by risk; only physical demand empties a shed. Until inventory follows, today reads as a risk premium being re-paid rather than a shortage arriving. There is also a dated counter-signal on the closure story itself: the US Treasury Secretary stated publicly that 17 million barrels of crude crossed Hormuz on Monday, which is not the throughput of a closed strait. Both readings are given here because the market has not reconciled them either.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. First, the 02-September official at 13:20 London: whether the flat spread tips into BACKWARDATION, which would be the first genuine prompt-tightness print of this cycle, or slips back into contango, which would mark today as a single geopolitical session. Second, whether warehouse stock finally moves - a second session of price strength on unchanged inventory weakens the tightness case rather than strengthening it. Third, the 16-September Federal Reserve decision, now close to a coin flip on a hike, which is the largest single scheduled risk to every industrial metal on this board. Fourth, the Q4 Japanese premium round, which conventionally opens in early September and has still not opened publicly.

lme.commentary:
THE 01-SEPTEMBER-2026 OFFICIAL IS THE FIRST NEW LME SETTLEMENT IN FIVE PUBLISHING DAYS, AND IT DID SOMETHING THIS PAGE HAS NOT PREVIOUSLY BEEN ABLE TO REPORT. Aluminium cash settled $3,261.00, up $39.00 or +1.21% on the 28-August official - the largest one-session cash gain since 11-August. The three-month settled $3,261.00, up $20.00 or +0.62%. Warehouse stock was unchanged at 246,725 tonnes. THE FULL CASH BOARD ON THE SAME SESSION, SO THE RANKING CAN BE CHECKED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST: aluminium +1.21% ($3,222.00 to $3,261.00), zinc +1.11% ($4,070.00 to $4,115.00), lead -0.32% ($1,880.00 to $1,874.00), copper -0.96% ($14,535.00 to $14,395.50), nickel -2.97% ($16,850.00 to $16,350.00). ALUMINIUM WAS THE STRONGEST METAL ON THE BOARD, WHICH EXACTLY INVERTS THE COMPLETED AUGUST MONTH THAT THIS PAGE REPORTED YESTERDAY. August's final monthly means ranked aluminium THIRD of five, beaten two-to-one by copper and two-and-a-half-to-one by zinc, on a month in which aluminium alone carried a Gulf supply premium, a smelter outage at roughly a tenth of world capacity, the largest alumina refinery outside China interrupted and two producer force majeures. The conclusion drawn from that was that the market had stopped paying for the disruption story. On the first session after that month closed, it paid.

THE CURVE IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE STORY AND IT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. Cash and three-month settled at the IDENTICAL number, so the spread is $0.00 - FLAT - against a $19.00 CONTANGO on 28-August. The mechanics are worth spelling out because they are what makes this different from a simple price rise: cash rose $39.00 while the forward rose only $20.00, so the front end firmed RELATIVE to the forward and the contango closed. Across the twenty published August sessions aluminium's cash mean of $3,249.63 sat BELOW its three-month mean of $3,251.23 - a $1.60 average CONTANGO sustained for a full month while the flat price rose 2.97%. This page read that combination, price up with the curve loosening, as a market lifted by macro and currency rather than by scarcity at the front. YESTERDAY PRODUCED THE OPPOSITE COMBINATION - price up 1.21% AND curve tightening $19.00 - and price and structure moving the same way is the scarcity signature. CROSS-BOARD CONTEXT ON THE IDENTICAL SESSION: copper settled a $180.50 BACKWARDATION, zinc a $178.00 BACKWARDATION, nickel a $325.00 CONTANGO, lead a $34.00 CONTANGO. Aluminium at flat has left the contango group without yet joining the backwardated one.

WHY THE CROSS-BOARD RANKING IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN COINCIDENCE. The macro on that session was actively hostile to every dollar-denominated industrial metal at once and through identical channels: money markets are pricing roughly a 70% probability of a US rate HIKE on 16-September, the global bond selloff has driven yields to their highest since 2008 - the 10-year JGB through 3%, the Australian 10-year at a fresh 15-year high, the Canadian 10-year at a 27-month high - gold has erased its entire 2026 gain, equities fell worldwide, and the LME fixing itself moved from 1.16460 on 28-August to 1.15930, a 0.46% stronger dollar. Copper and nickel obeyed all of it. Aluminium rose 1.21% into it. A shared shock that pushes four metals down and one up isolates the differentiator by construction, and the only differentiator aluminium has is the roughly 9% of world primary supply that exits through the Strait of Hormuz - where two oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Monday night and the United States struck Iranian targets around the waterway in reply, with Brent rising a third consecutive session above $95 to a near six-week high.

THE STANDING OBJECTION, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS PAGE RAISES ITS BULL WEIGHT BY FOUR POINTS RATHER THAN FIFTEEN. NOT ONE TONNE LEFT AN LME WAREHOUSE. Aluminium stock printed 246,725 t for a third consecutive published session and has moved 200 tonnes in total across the thirteen published sessions since 17-August; the draw did not decelerate, it stopped, and it stopped more than two weeks ago. On the same session copper's warehouse stock fell again, from 234,275 t to 233,500 t, and copper's price FELL. A price and a curve can be moved by risk; only physical offtake empties a shed. There is also a dated counter-signal on the closure narrative itself, from the US government rather than from a market commentator: Treasury Secretary Bessent stated that 17 MILLION BARRELS of crude passed through Hormuz on Monday, the same day the tankers were hit. Both things are true - the waterway is dangerous enough to strike ships in and open enough to move near-normal volume - and what the market bought was disruption PROBABILITY rather than realised disruption.

SOURCING AND STALENESS, DISCLOSED BECAUSE IT AFFECTS HOW THIS BOARD SHOULD BE READ. The 01-September board was taken from the English Westmetall overview and cross-verified on the cache-busted German overview; the two agree line for line across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three EUR/USD fixings, and the 31-August column correctly carries a dash for the UK Summer Bank Holiday. The overviews are used because two independent language versions agree and because the entire board rolls together; the tables are expected to catch up within a day. Today's 02-September official prints at 13:20 London, after this page is compiled, and it is the confirmation test: a backwardated print would be the first genuine prompt-tightness signal of this cycle, a re-widening contango would mark yesterday as one geopolitical session and nothing structural.

THE POLICY DEPENDENCY IS THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS ROW - roughly 77% of the delivered premium is Section 232 duty at the current cash price, so the principal risk to it is not physical and not American demand; it is a signature in Washington. drivers.text: Section 232 verified at 50% on articles, 25% on derivatives - and the carve-out structure matters — Re-verified against the primary source this run rather than carried. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085 on 04-June-2026 and effective 08-June-2026, leaves the Annex I-A rate on aluminium articles at 50% and the Annex I-B derivative rate at 25%, with a 15% temporary subset for fixed industrial machinery and power equipment now extended to agricultural equipment and residential HVAC. THE ANNEX I-C CARVE-OUT LIST IS THE PART MOST OFTEN MISREAD: for Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Japan, Korea, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, Taiwan, the United Kingdom and any EU member state, the effective rate is set by the product's HTSUS Column 1 duty - 15% total where Column 1 is below 15%, and no Section 232 addition where Column 1 is at or above 15%. Canada and Mexico under USMCA pay 25% on non-US content only, with a 15% floor. The US-origin content threshold was lowered from 95% to 85% by weight.
drivers.source: Federal Register - Proclamation 11032, 91 FR 34085, further adjusting the tariff regimes for aluminum, steel and copper, effective 08-Jun-2026

drivers.text: The US-Canada framework is reported, not law - and it already moved the premium 8.2% in one session — A tentative framework that would cut US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25% was reported on 19-August-2026. It is NOT finalised, NOT across the board, and different rates may apply to some derivative products. THE MARKET EFFECT WAS IMMEDIATE AND MEASURABLE: Platts marked the September Midwest transaction premium down 8.2% to 95.0 c/lb on 20-August, with October and November contracts down more than 12%. That is an unconfirmed policy headline moving a physical premium by more in a day than the physical market moved all month, which is the clearest available evidence of how policy-dominated this benchmark is. The European read-across is publicly flagged: Canadian metal redirected to Europe during the 50% regime would flow back to the US, tightening America and loosening Rotterdam at the same time.
drivers.source: Fastmarkets - European aluminium market watchful of proposed US-Canada tariff reduction, 24-Aug-2026

drivers.text: The Q4-2026 Japanese round opens now, into a spot market trading below the record Q3 settlement — Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July-2026, a record, up 12.4% on Q2's $351.50/t. What is publicly documented is the spot backdrop, and it is unhelpful for sellers: MJP spot peaked in Q2, inflected down from July and kept falling through August, trading notably below the $395 benchmark with sellers struggling to transact and buyers holding out. A spot market below the prevailing quarterly settlement going into the quarter that settlement covers is the standard set-up for a lower next round. drivers.text: Freight is the live inflation inside every delivered premium, and both Middle East chokepoints are impaired — The Baltic Dry Index closed at 3,186 on 28-August-2026, up 2.54% on the day, its seventh consecutive gain and its highest since 02-June - up 12.1% on the week, 21.05% on the month and 57.33% on the year, led by Capesize at 5,336. With Chinese smelter margins up 87.7% year on year and 100% of operating capacity profitable, cheaper alumina removes the last cost-side mechanism that could have forced anyone to curtail. Every tonne that can run, runs. China's domestic alumina at RMB 2,600-2,700 against a national weighted full cost of RMB 2,718/t is the one floor in the system, and it is a floor under ALUMINA, not under aluminium.

BAUXITE IS THE ONE UPSTREAM LEG STILL POINTING UP, ON FLOW DATA RATHER THAN ON A PRICE. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THIS ROW ESCALATED AGAIN AND IT IS THE PROXIMATE CAUSE OF TODAY'S ALUMINIUM MOVE. The sequence, all dated: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on LARAK ISLAND on Sunday 30-August; Iran retaliated against US bases; on MONDAY NIGHT 31-AUGUST two oil tankers - one Saudi Arabian, one South Korean - were struck by projectiles inside the Strait within minutes of each other, reported by the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre with no casualties or environmental impact; the US then struck Iranian targets around the Strait, which President Trump described as retaliation for Iranian attempts to lay mines in the waterway and for the earlier attack on a US base, threatening a significantly larger response to further Iranian action; Iran said it had already responded against US bases and fired missiles toward Jordan. Qatar's foreign ministry said on Tuesday it would re-intensify mediation, and Iran's president said Tehran would return to talks if Washington moved that way. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS EQUALLY DATED AND IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT RATHER THAN BURIED, BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THE TWO EITHER: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that 17 MILLION BARRELS of crude passed through Hormuz on Monday - the same day the tankers were hit - and offered it as evidence that Tehran does not control the waterway. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ALUMINIUM SPECIFICALLY: roughly 9% of global primary supply exits via this waterway and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. Brent rose a third consecutive session above $95 on it, and aluminium led the LME board while copper and nickel fell. THE HONEST FRAMING: what is being priced is disruption PROBABILITY, not realised disruption, and the Iran-Oman safe-corridor announcement of 26-August shows how fast that probability can be re-rated in either direction - it moved this page's scenario weights once and then broke down within four days.

headlines.title: ALUMINIUM WAS THE STRONGEST METAL ON THE BOARD AS THE LME REOPENED - cash $3,261.00 up 1.21%, the largest one-session gain since 11-August, while copper fell 0.96% and nickel 2.97% on the same session. The 01-September official is the first new settlement in five publishing days. The completed August month had ranked aluminium THIRD of five; the first session after that month closed inverted the ranking entirely.

THE CONTANGO CLOSED TO ZERO - cash and three-month both settled $3,261.00 against a $19.00 contango on 28-August. Price UP and curve TIGHTENING is the opposite combination to August, when a $1.60 average contango was held for twenty sessions while the flat price rose 2.97%. Price and structure moving together is the scarcity signature. Copper settled a $180.50 backwardation and zinc a $178.00 backwardation on the same board.

TWO OIL TANKERS STRUCK INSIDE THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ ON MONDAY NIGHT - one Saudi Arabian, one South Korean, hit by projectiles within minutes of each other, reported by the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre with no casualties. The US then struck Iranian targets around the Strait in retaliation for attempted mine-laying; Iran responded against US bases and fired missiles toward Jordan; Qatar has re-intensified mediation. Roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through this waterway.

THE STRAIT IS NOT ACTUALLY CLOSED, ON THE US TREASURY'S OWN NUMBERS - Secretary Bessent stated that 17 MILLION BARRELS of crude passed through Hormuz on Monday, the same day two tankers were struck, offering it as evidence Tehran does not control the waterway. Both facts are true simultaneously and the market has not reconciled them: dangerous enough to hit tankers, open enough to move near-normal volume. What is being priced is disruption PROBABILITY, not realised disruption.

BRENT ABOVE $95 FOR A THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION at $95.37 (+0.78% day, +13.86% month, +41.10% year), a near six-week high, with WTI $90.75, thermal coal $144.85 at an eleven-week high (+2.19%) and TTF gas EUR 73.93 (+2.36%). Two-sided for aluminium: energy at these levels is margin-negative across smelting, refining and freight, and is simultaneously the channel through which the Gulf risk premium reaches the metal.

MARKETS NOW PRICE ROUGHLY A 70% CHANCE OF A US RATE HIKE ON 16-SEPTEMBER after the Fed chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut, and the global bond selloff has taken yields to their highest since 2008 - US 10-year 4.808%, UK 5.225%, JGB through 3%, Australia 5.196% at a fresh 15-year high, Canada at a 27-month high. Gold has erased its entire 2026 gain and equities fell worldwide. Higher real rates raise the carry cost of financing warehouse metal and compress the demand path under every deficit forecast on this page.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCK DID NOT MOVE - 246,725 t for a third consecutive published session and 200 tonnes in total across thirteen sessions since 17-August. Copper's stock fell again on the same session and copper's price fell. A price and a curve can be moved by risk; only offtake empties a warehouse. Until inventory follows, today is a risk premium and not a shortage.

CHINESE INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORY FELL TO 837,000 t ON 31-AUGUST, down 15,000 t on the prior Thursday, 106,000 t across August and 278,000 t from the early-July peak - a counter-seasonal destock that SMM expects to continue through the first half of September. This is the strongest genuinely physical bullish datapoint available publicly, and it is the one that does NOT appear in the LME warehouse row.

THE SUPPLY-RETURN TIMETABLE IS DATED, PUBLIC AND UNCHANGED - EGA's Al Taweelah at 25% of cells (315 of 1,262) with pre-war output reaffirmed for Q1-2027; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015; Alcoa's San Ciprian complete; Slovalco resuming 75 kt from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals restarting 75 kt by end-2026; Alunorte ramping back to FULL. This is the standing cap on any recovery and it did not change today.

TWO GULF LOSSES REMAIN UNDATED, WHICH IS MORE THAN CAN BE SAID FOR ANY RETURN ON THE LIST - Qatalum at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding, and Alba's reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idle since March 2026, 19% of 1,623 kt, with a stated intention to REPLACE rather than restart them.

BALTIC DRY SNAPPED A SEVEN-SESSION WINNING RUN, falling 0.91% to 3,157 on Tuesday, with Capesize - the ore-and-bauxite segment - down 2.1% to 5,221 and also ending a seven-day run, while Panamax rose 1.9% to 2,360 for a seventh consecutive gain. The level is the story rather than the day: +11.04% on the month, +58.96% on the year, and the largest single input-cost inflation in the bauxite and alumina legs of this chain.

SECTION 232 RE-VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES under Proclamation 11032, 91 FR 34085, effective 08-June-2026. At today's $3,261.00 cash official the duty leg alone is $1,630.50/t - roughly 78% of a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t. CHINA'S AUGUST SURVEYS STILL DISAGREE AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS UNRESOLVED - the official NBS manufacturing PMI at 49.8, in contraction for a second month, against the private RatingDog index at 51.5, a substantial beat. Falling social inventory is the better evidence and it points the other way.

Alumina loosening is bullish for smelter margins and bearish for metal: with Chinese smelter margins up 87.7% year on year and 100% of operating capacity profitable, there is no cost-side mechanism anywhere forcing a curtailment.

Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. status.status: SAN CIPRIAN RESTART COMPLETE; PORTLAND POWER SECURED TO MID-2035; SOUTH32 ACQUISITION SIGNED, CLOSE GUIDED H1-2027
status.update: The San Ciprian smelter restart COMPLETED ON 07-APRIL-2026 and was the primary reason Alcoa's Q2-2026 aluminium production rose 5% quarter on quarter to 636 kt. Portland in Victoria is operating with power secured to mid-2035 through a 300 MW AGL contract plus a nine-year 287 MW contract that took effect 01-JULY-2026; combined, those support up to 95% of the 358 ktpa nameplate against a recent running rate near 80%. THE SOUTH32 TRANSACTION IS THE LARGER STRUCTURAL ITEM: announced 30-June-2026 at $4.1bn ($3.1bn cash plus about 17.0m Alcoa shares), an implied enterprise value near $4.7bn including assumed lease debt, plus a contingent value right worth up to $750m tied to alumina and aluminium price strikes. It adds roughly 18 Mt of attributable bauxite and 5 Mt of attributable alumina annually and raises Alcoa's smelting capacity by about 26%. status.name: Rio Tinto (RIO) / Tomago
status.status: SECURED - GOVERNMENT SUPPORT PACKAGE AND A 10-YEAR PPA TO 2038

status.status: RESTARTS CONFIRMED - 75 kt EACH, BOTH LANDING BY OR IN Q4-2026
status.update: Both restarts remain on their published timetable and neither is speculative. Together with Century's completed Mt Holly expansion, Alcoa's completed San Ciprian and Portland restarts and EGA's Al Taweelah ramp, these constitute a Western supply-restoration pipeline that is dated, published and already partly delivered. THE MARKET IMPLICATION IS THE ONE THIS PAGE HAS MADE ALL MONTH AND THE COMPLETED AUGUST BOARD SUPPORTS IT: the disruption premium is being unwound on a schedule the market can read, which is why aluminium's monthly average gain of 2.97% finished third of five behind metals with no disruption story at all.

status.name: China operators (aggregate, incl. Chalco and Hongqiao)
status.status: AT OR THROUGH THE 45 Mt POLICY CEILING; OUTPUT STABLE, MARGINS WIDE, EXPORTS ELEVATED

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES - VERIFIED; A US-CANADA CUT TO 25% IS REPORTED BUT NOT LAW
status.impact: Mixed (the largest single swing factor in the US delivered premium)
status.update: Verified against the primary source this run. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085 and effective 08-June-2026, holds the Annex I-A rate on aluminium articles at 50% and the Annex I-B derivative rate at 25%, with a 15% temporary subset now extended to agricultural equipment and residential HVAC, and aluminium lithographic plates newly brought into coverage. Annex I-C sets a 15% effective ceiling for a listed group including Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU member states, 10% where derivative aluminium content is entirely US-smelted and cast, and 25% on non-US content only for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican goods with a 15% floor. THE PENDING CHANGE IS REPORTED, NOT ENACTED: a tentative framework to halve the Canadian rate to 25% was reported 19-August and drove an 8.2% single-session collapse in the September Midwest premium to 95.0 c/lb on 20-August. trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN, AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN A CALENDAR DATE: the Strait of Hormuz de-escalation that this page carried from 26-August - an Iran-Oman announcement of a planned safe maritime corridor - BROKE DOWN OVER THE WEEKEND. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, adjacent to the Strait, on Sunday 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; and the IRGC has claimed that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Reporting on 31-August describes the renewed hostilities as having dashed hopes of near-term normalisation of transit, and Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it while the LME was closed. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT AND IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated that strikes against Iran would be LIMITED and that the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large volumes of oil moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and attributed the Iranian action to sanctions pressure. THE TWO READS ARE NOT RECONCILED HERE BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM EITHER, and no LME session has yet had the opportunity to express a view. SECOND STRUCTURAL POINT, UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE BUT NOW SIMULTANEOUS WITH THE FIRST: Bab el Mandeb transits are down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and US MARAD advisory 2026-006 remains in force through 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Both Middle East chokepoints are impaired at the same time, which leaves a Gulf or Red Sea shipper with no unimpaired routing to Europe and is the physical reason freight is inflating faster than any other cost on this page. THIRD, THE SANCTIONS CLOCK: the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026, and the EU import ban on Russian aluminium takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026 - a dated, certain change to the availability of the metal that dominates LME warrantable stock.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.

flows.note: RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL - AND IT IS THE CONFIRMATION TEST FOR EVERYTHING ON THIS PAGE. Yesterday's 01-September print did three things at once: cash rose 1.21% to $3,261.00, the $19.00 contango closed to $0.00, and the three-month settled exactly at the weekly 38.2% retracement of the 2,300-to-3,855 advance while clearing the daily 38.2% at $3,254.60 that had been rejected nine times. THE SPECIFIC THING TO WATCH IS THE SPREAD, NOT THE PRICE. A print of cash ABOVE three-month would be the first genuine BACKWARDATION of this cycle and the first prompt-tightness signal the physical story has produced. A re-widening contango marks yesterday as one geopolitical session. THE SECOND TEST IS INVENTORY: stock has printed 246,725 t for three consecutive sessions and moved 200 tonnes in thirteen. A second session of price strength on unchanged inventory WEAKENS the tightness case rather than strengthening it.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - NOW CLOSE TO A COIN FLIP ON A HIKE AND THE LARGEST SINGLE SCHEDULED RISK TO EVERY METAL ON THIS BOARD. Money markets price roughly a 70% probability of a 25 basis-point INCREASE, following the chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut on 28-August and the statement that inflation is not slowing meaningfully. The repricing has already driven global yields to their highest since 2008 and erased gold's entire 2026 gain. WHY IT MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY FOR ALUMINIUM RIGHT NOW: the curve is flat at $0.00, and the economics of holding physical metal against a flat curve are decided entirely by funding cost. A hike makes storage unprofitable at parity and pressures holders toward selling rather than carrying, which is the mechanism that would reverse yesterday's spread move without any change in the physical position.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM ROUND CONVENTIONALLY OPENS IN EARLY SEPTEMBER - WHICH IS NOW - AND HAS NOT OPENED PUBLICLY. No offers, no bids, no settlement have appeared in free reporting. The Q3-2026 benchmark of $395/t CIF Japan, assessed 06-July-2026 by S&P Global Platts, was a record and is carried unchanged; it settled 12.4% above Q2's $351.50/t against producer opening offers of $480/t from South32 and $460/t from Rio Tinto. THE PENDING QUARTER IS SHOWN WITH A NULL VALUE AND A SCENARIO RANGE OF $310-400 RATHER THAN A NUMBER, bounded below by publicly documented MJP spot trading beneath the benchmark since July and above by the record Q3 level itself. A SPECIFIC CROSS-CHECK WARNING: results quoting $98-103/t offers with buyers bidding in the $80s are Q4-2025 data and are a full year stale.

US NON-FARM PAYROLLS FOR AUGUST - THE SINGLE HIGHEST-WEIGHT INPUT INTO THE 16-SEPTEMBER FED DECISION, LANDING INTO A MARKET THAT HAS ALREADY REPRICED TO ROUGHLY 70% FOR A HIKE. The asymmetry is worth stating in advance because it is unusual: with a hike already the majority-priced outcome, a hot print largely confirms what is in the curve, while a soft print has room to unwind a great deal of the bond selloff and the dollar strength that came with it. For an industrial metal that is the more consequential tail, and it is the one currently underweighted in positioning. Treat any pre-release estimate circulating in free reporting as an estimate.

FASTMARKETS INTERNATIONAL ALUMINIUM, 40TH EDITION - the industry's principal Q4 pricing-and-contracting gathering, with a published agenda covering emerging supply regions and Indonesia's expanding role, upstream bauxite and alumina risk, logistics, recycling growth and low-carbon aluminium. IT MATTERS COMMERCIALLY BECAUSE OF ITS TIMING RATHER THAN ITS CONTENT: it sits directly on top of the Q4 premium negotiation window and immediately before the Fed decision, and annual-contract direction for 2027 is conventionally set around it. Public read-outs from the event are usually the first free indication of where Q4 and calendar-2027 premium expectations have landed.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - AND IT INTERACTS DIRECTLY WITH THE INVENTORY ROW ON THIS PAGE. LME warehouse stock has flatlined at 246,725 t, and the available tonnage sitting on that number is disproportionately Russian-origin. The LME has required attestations to warrant Russian metal in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026. WHAT THAT MEANS PRACTICALLY: headline LME stock overstates the metal that is actually deliverable into European consumption after year end, so a flat headline inventory is a weaker comfort than it looks, and any re-warranting or relocation ahead of the deadline can move the reported number without any change in real availability. This is the main reason the inventory row is read alongside Chinese social inventory rather than on its own.

US MARAD ADVISORY 2026-006 ON THE RED SEA AND BAB EL MANDEB CORRIDOR REACHES ITS STATED EXPIRY - a scheduled decision point on whether the second impaired Middle East chokepoint is de-rated or extended. Transits remain down roughly 24% since the July Houthi blockade and carriers continue routing via the Cape, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. WHY IT SITS ON AN ALUMINIUM PAGE: with Hormuz now the site of physical strikes on tankers, there is no unimpaired routing between Gulf and Asian production and European consumption, and the resulting delivered-cost inflation lands inside every regional premium simultaneously while remaining invisible in the LME flat price. No war-risk insurance reprice has been published since the strikes, so the 7.5-10%-of-hull-value mark from 22-July should be read as a floor.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD, AND THE CLOSED AUGUST MONTH IS NOW THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE ARGUMENT. The timetable is public and it advanced again this week: EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells - 315 of 1,262, up from roughly 18% a week ago - with all three potlines being worked and full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027; Century's Mt Holly is at FULL capacity for the first time since 2015, adding nearly 10% to total US primary output; Alcoa's San Ciprian restart completed in April and Portland has power secured to mid-2035; Hydro's Slovalco resumes 75 kt from Q4-2026 and Magnitude 7 Metals restarts 75 kt at Marston by end-2026; Tomago is underwritten to 2038 by a government package and a 10-year PPA. A CORRECTION MADE OPENLY THIS RUN REINFORCES THE POINT: this page had carried Alunorte at roughly 50% of capacity, but Hydro announced on 13-August that it was ramping the 6.3 Mtpa refinery back to FULL after ANP approved it as a gas self-importer. The largest alumina refinery outside China is not a live constraint. THE PRICE ALREADY KNOWS: aluminium's completed August monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, and its curve averaged a $1.60 contango against copper's $197.67 backwardation.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED, AND THE COMPLETED MONTH NOW SHOWS EXACTLY WHEN IT STOPPED. LME aluminium warehouse stock fell from 262,650 t on 03-August to 246,925 t on 17-August and then moved 200 TONNES ACROSS THE FINAL NINE SESSIONS OF THE MONTH, closing at 246,725 t. The draw did not decelerate gradually - it halted, and it halted three weeks before the month ended. August's average stock of 251,215 t against July's 282,350 t is an 11.0% monthly decline, which is real but ranks THIRD of five: copper -22.6%, zinc -14.3%, aluminium -11.0%, nickel -2.2%, lead +8.9%. A DEFICIT NARRATIVE REQUIRES INVENTORY TO KEEP FALLING; this one has flatlined at a level that is historically low but no longer directional, while the metal sitting on it is disproportionately Russian-origin ahead of a 31-December-2026 EU import ban. THE ONE GENUINE COUNTERWEIGHT IS CHINESE AND IT IS CONSTRUCTIVE: ingot social inventory fell to 837,000 t on 31-August, down 15,000 t on the prior Thursday and 23,000 t on the prior Monday, for a cumulative August destock of 106,000 t and 278,000 t off the early-July peak - counter-seasonal, and SMM expects it to continue through the first half of September.

GULF SUPPLY DISRUPTION IS REAL AND PARTLY UNDATED - AND ON 01-SEPTEMBER THE MARKET STARTED PAYING FOR IT AGAIN. THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN THIS RUN, MEANING THE RISK THAT THE DISRUPTION STORY GOES UNPAID IS RECEDING RATHER THAN THE DISRUPTION ITSELF BEING RESOLVED. The evidence is one dated session and it is unusually clean: aluminium cash rose 1.21% to $3,261.00 and led the entire LME board while copper fell 0.96% and nickel 2.97% on the SAME session and the SAME hostile macro, and the $19.00 contango closed to zero. When a shared macro pushes four metals down and one up, the one going up is being bid for something the others do not have. THE TRIGGER WAS DATED AND PHYSICAL: two oil tankers, one Saudi and one South Korean, were struck by projectiles inside the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night per the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre; the US struck Iranian targets around the Strait in retaliation for attempted mine-laying; Iran responded against US bases and fired missiles toward Jordan; Brent rose a third consecutive session above $95. THE PHYSICAL POSITION UNDERNEATH HAS NOT MOVED IN MONTHS: Qatalum at roughly 60% of 648 kt on reduced gas with NO published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba's reduction Lines 1-3 idle since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with a stated intention to REPLACE rather than restart. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS DATED TOO AND IS NOT SUPPRESSED: the US Treasury Secretary stated that 17 million barrels of crude crossed Hormuz on Monday, which is not the throughput of a closed strait. What is being priced is disruption probability, not realised disruption - and probability premia unwind faster than shortages do.

PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON, AND CHINA'S OWN SURVEYS NOW DISAGREE ABOUT WHETHER IT IS COMING. TREND HELD AT DOWN, BECAUSE THE HARD INVENTORY DATA IS THE ONE SERIES POINTING THE RIGHT WAY. The official NBS manufacturing PMI printed 49.8 for August, up from 49.2 but in contraction for a second month, with employment at 48.7 and non-manufacturing at 49.0; the private RatingDog index printed 51.5 against 50.9 expected, a substantial beat. The official panel skews to large state heavy industry and the private one to smaller exporters, and they have diverged repeatedly through 2026, so the August China demand signal is UNRESOLVED rather than positive. China's aluminium PROCESSING composite PMI is unambiguous, though, at 48.7% - up slightly but still contracting, with September expected to return to expansion. PV frame operating rates are strong on POLICY-DRIVEN advance stockpiling ahead of an expected US Section 232 solar rule rather than on end demand, with forward oversupply pressure behind it. Against all of that, ingot social inventory keeps falling counter-seasonally and European foil deliveries rose 5.8% quarter on quarter in Q2. The physical draw is the better evidence and it is why this trend stays down.

MACRO AND RATES OVERWHELM THE MICRO - HELD AT UP AND NOW THE SINGLE LARGEST BEARISH FORCE ON THIS PAGE, WITH A DATED SCHEDULED EVENT ATTACHED TO IT. Money markets are pricing roughly a 70% PROBABILITY OF A 25 BASIS-POINT US RATE HIKE ON 16-SEPTEMBER, after the Federal Reserve chair's hawkish Jackson Hole debut on 28-August and his statement that inflation is not slowing meaningfully; ECB officials are separately reported to be leaning toward a September hike. THE GLOBAL BOND SELLOFF HAS DRIVEN YIELDS TO THEIR HIGHEST SINCE 2008: US 10-year 4.808%, UK 5.225%, the 10-year JGB THROUGH 3% at 3.014%, the Australian 10-year at 5.196% and a fresh 15-YEAR HIGH, the German 10-year 3.339%, the Canadian 10-year at a 27-month high. Gold has erased its entire 2026 gain and equity indices fell worldwide - Nikkei -2.89%, ASX 200 -1.81%, Shanghai -0.82%. EVERY TRANSMISSION CHANNEL RUNS THE WRONG WAY FOR AN INDUSTRIAL METAL: higher real rates raise the cost of financing physical inventory, which is the mechanism that turns a flat or contangoed curve into forced selling rather than into profitable storage; they compress the demand outlook that every deficit forecast on this page depends on; and a firmer dollar - DXY 99.798, and a 0.46% stronger dollar between the 28-August and 01-September LME fixings - mechanically lowers a dollar-denominated price. THE ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS RISK READ SLIGHTLY DIFFERENTLY TODAY: aluminium rose 1.21% straight into all of it, which says the metal-specific bid was strong enough to overwhelm the macro for one session. One session.

INPUT-COST INFLATION THROUGH FREIGHT, CARBON AND BAUXITE - HELD AT UP, WITH TWO NEW DATED POINTS THIS RUN. The carbon chain turned: a large Shandong smelter set its SEPTEMBER prebaked anode tender at RMB 5,730/t, UP RMB 100 month on month, ending four months of drift; and PetroChina raised low-sulphur petroleum coke list prices at ALL FIVE of its North-East China refineries effective 00:00 on 01-September. SMM's cost note adds that fluoride salts rose through August with further increases expected in September, and that coal gains will push September power tariffs moderately higher. Freight is the largest single inflation: the Baltic Dry Index closed at 3,186 on 28-August, its seventh consecutive gain and highest since 02-June, up 21.05% on the month and 57.33% on the year, Capesize-led - which is the ore-and-bauxite end. Imported bauxite CIF is the driver SMM names behind rising Chinese alumina costs. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, AND IT IS LARGE: SMM puts China's weighted all-in production cost DOWN 0.7% month on month and 3.4% year on year in August, with an average smelter margin of RMB 7,890/t - up 87.7% year on year - and 100% of operating capacity profitable. A RMB 100/t anode increase against a RMB 7,890/t margin is a rounding item, which is precisely why cost inflation is a margin risk and not a supply-side price support.

ALUMINA LOOSENS FASTER THAN METAL AND THE SMELTER MARGIN STOPS BEING A CONSTRAINT ON ANYONE'S OUTPUT - TREND SET TO DOWN THIS RUN, MEANING THE RISK OF AN ALUMINA-DRIVEN COST SQUEEZE IS FALLING RATHER THAN THE RISK ITSELF BEING BENIGN. The SMM Alumina Index averaged RMB 2,695/t across the 26-July to 25-August window, DOWN 1.8% month on month; 30,000 t traded at $379/mt FOB Indonesia on 31-August for October shipment; Hydro's Alunorte is ramping back to full after its August gas interruption rather than sitting at 50%; EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is at roughly 50% and rising. THE CONSEQUENCE IS BEARISH FOR METAL EVEN THOUGH IT IS BULLISH FOR SMELTERS, and the distinction is the point: with 100% of Chinese operating capacity profitable and margins up 87.7% year on year, there is no cost-side mechanism anywhere in the world forcing a curtailment. Every tonne that can run, runs. China's domestic alumina at RMB 2,600-2,700 against a national weighted full cost of RMB 2,718/t is the one floor in the system, and it is a floor under alumina, not under aluminium.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE DELIVERED PREMIUM MORE THAN THE PHYSICAL MARKET DOES, AND THE PRICED-IN RELIEF HAS NOT BEEN ENACTED. HELD AT UP. Section 232 is verified at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives under Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, 91 FR 34085. At the 28-August cash official of $3,222.00 that is $1,611/t of pure duty, which is roughly 77% of a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t - the American premium is predominantly a policy variable, not a tightness variable. THE EVIDENCE IS A SINGLE SESSION: an unconfirmed report on 19-August that the US would halve the Canadian rate to 25% took the September Midwest transaction premium DOWN 8.2% to 95.0 c/lb the next day, with October and November down more than 12%, while nothing physical changed. The framework is still not law and not across the board. THE EUROPEAN READ-ACROSS IS THE SECOND-ORDER RISK AND IT IS PUBLICLY FLAGGED: Canadian metal redirected to Europe during the 50% regime flows back to the US if the rate halves, tightening America and loosening Rotterdam simultaneously.

BOTH MIDDLE EAST CHOKEPOINTS ARE IMPAIRED SIMULTANEOUSLY AND THE HORMUZ LEG ESCALATED FROM THREAT TO PHYSICAL STRIKE - LIKELIHOOD AND IMPACT BOTH RAISED TO HIGH THIS RUN, TREND HELD AT UP. The escalation is no longer rhetorical: TWO OIL TANKERS WERE STRUCK BY PROJECTILES INSIDE THE STRAIT on Monday night per the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, the US carried out retaliatory strikes on Iranian targets around the waterway in response to attempted mine-laying, President Trump threatened a significantly larger response to further Iranian action, and Iran fired on US bases and toward Jordan. Bab el Mandeb transits remain down roughly 24% since the July Houthi blockade with US MARAD advisory 2026-006 in force through 22-September; Suez traffic remains far below pre-crisis normal with carriers routing via the Cape and adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. NO WAR-RISK INSURANCE REPRICING HAS BEEN PUBLISHED SINCE THE STRIKES, so the 7.5-10%-of-hull-value mark from 22-July - against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm - should be treated as a FLOOR rather than a current quote, and a hull-value premium is the first thing that moves after tankers are physically hit. This is a delivered-cost risk that sits inside every regional premium on this page at once and is invisible in the LME flat price. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS THE 17 MILLION BARRELS that the US Treasury says crossed on Monday: the corridor is dangerous, not shut.

The LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026 and the EU import ban takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026, against Russian-origin metal dominating available LME stock. THE COMMERCIAL POINT IS THAT UNRESOLVED RULES FOUR MONTHS BEFORE A START DATE ARE THEMSELVES A COST: they force optionality into contracts, widen bid-offer on anything crossing a carbon border, and fall hardest on producers whose verification chain is not already built.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
